prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pull live local search results from the web right now, but I can tell you the fastest ways to find qualified backflow testing and repair near Liberty, MO, what to check for, and roughly what it should cost.

How to find providers
- Contact the City of Liberty Utilities / Public Works — they usually keep a list of approved or registered backflow testers and can tell you local rules for required testing and reporting. Search the city website for “backflow” or “cross-connection control.”
- Search local plumbing and irrigation companies in the Liberty/Kansas City area (Google Maps, Yelp, Angi, Nextdoor). Look for “backflow testing,” “RPZ testing,” or “backflow prevention assembly tester.”
- Look for companies that advertise “backflow testing” specifically (many general plumbers, irrigation companies, and specialty backflow firms provide testing & repairs).
- Professional directories: American Backflow Prevention Association (ABPA) or state plumbing boards may list certified testers or training providers.

What to verify before hiring
- Certification: Ask if the technician is a certified/backflow prevention assembly tester and which certification they hold. (“Backflow tester” or RPZ tester certification.)
- Licensing & insurance: Confirm the company is licensed to work in Missouri and carries liability insurance.
- Reporting: Ask if they complete and submit the test report to the City of Liberty (cities often require the tester to file results).
- Experience with your type of device (RPZ, reduced pressure, double check, pressure vacuum breaker, irrigation backflow, etc.).
- Warranty on repairs and whether replacement parts are new and meet manufacturer specs.

Typical costs (approximate)
- Test only: $50–$150 per device (depends on device type and region).
- Repairs: small repairs $100–$300; larger repairs or replacement assemblies $300–$1,500+ depending on parts and labor.
- Travel/minimum charges may apply.

Sample questions to ask a company when you call
- “Are you certified to test backflow prevention assemblies in Missouri? Can you provide your tester certification number?”
- “Will you file the test report with the City of Liberty or do I need to?”
- “What’s your price to test this device (give device type/location)?”
- “Do you provide on-site repairs and give an estimate before starting work?”

- Help you evaluate a few company names if you paste them here (I can tell you what to ask/check).
- If you’d like me to find specific businesses, tell me you want a web search and I’ll explain how to run it quickly (I can’t browse myself).
